# Preface {.unnumbered}

This book should not exist.
There are already many free available materials online.
Many universities provide materials and open courses.
Publishers have free books and PDFs available.
Good deaders have shared teaching and tutorial on video sharing platform and social media^[some might be more legitimate than others].
I also hope you have access to libraries where you are.
For Malagasy scholars, in my personal experience, foreign colleagues do not mind bringing books. Just ask within reasons.
And ultimately, I expect that the major part of what is written here are taught during undergraduate and graduate courses at your institutions.

So, is there a need for this book? Well, I  try to address superficial problems with this book.
The first problem is fragmented information.
There are books on coding, statistics, mathematics, some are more foundational, some are applied.
But, if you reading a statistics book and bump into an unfamiliar math concept, searching for an appropriate math book is not trivial. Likewise, if there is a specific R packages for, finding the complementary stat book is not trivial.
In any case, there is a need to search information on a different source hoping that it would align with level and context.
So one goal in this handbook is to gather in multiple knowledge on mathematics, statistcs, and coding in one place with an attempt to complement each other.

The second problem is that many books are dense and formal.
The main idea is to focus on the applied side whether it is mathematics, statistics or coding.
While there is a section on formal definition^[which can always be google, there here for complementarity], most parts focus on intuition, examples, and advices.
Each topic in short dedicated digestable chapter.
The format is designed to promote active-learning.

The third problem is most books are written by non-Malagasy scholars meaning that it is based on a diffeent perspesctive and view.
While this book is written in english^[a Malagasy version is cooking but that requires a body of work], the targeted audience are Malagasy students and researchers.
The context and examples could be easier to grasp if it aligns with Malagasy way of thinking and experience. For instance, it is natural for Malagasy to understand traveling from Antsiranana to Toalagnaro than from New York to San Francisco. Or using a Malagasy idioms.
Most of the intution, examples, and metaphors carry Malagasy flavor^[Madagascar is quite a diverse place, it should be more conservative and say based on my experience in environment where I grew up].

The final problem is Malagasy cannot afford books.
This is free book, you can download it, use it as you wish, and share it.
Be aware that is self-edited book so you should not use it as a valid citation.
As the proverb says, *Saonjo iray lohasa, tsy laozan'izay mamara*.
Someone might try to make a business out of it. I am sorry for those who will pay for it and get scammed.


As a warning, it is worth mentioning that I am no expert in any of the topics and sections.
I am mostly self-taught training in statistics and programming.
There are experts in the field and they should be the absolute reference.
This book is based on my own experience and the way how I understand the concept, the way how I code.
This is more a generalist approach hoping the facilite converstation among mathematician, statisticians, programmers, especially data-driven researcher. I am not sure I failed, but I am not confident I succeeded.

The emergence of AI might also render this book obsolete. It could address most superficial problem above.I used AI to edit and format the texts, the code, and sanity check. As a sceptic, many features are useful. However, I would also poist that as I researcher, honing skills, original ideas are essential. Most crucial, over-dependence on tools unware of its own mistake is . As far as I know, learning requires doing the right but also the wrong thing, and repeat until enough experience

This book is a tool, indeed trying to address superficial problems, I leave to each and everyone to address the real issue: grit.


### Structure and usage {.unnumbered}

This current version contains three parts: basic mathematics, basic statistics, and basic coding. Each chapter shares the same format:

- Intuition: it starts with a short quote hoping to help understand or remember the main idea and text elaborating on the topic.
- Formal definition: this part can be found in any textbook, and is here for complementarity and formality
- Examples
- Tips and warning
- A fifth section to explain terminology

This is R, and code, output.
Don't be frustrated if repetitive,(one concept in anther chapter). This is part of learning but also, there is no expectation that you will read each chapter, so reminded as it appears

Codes are omitted on in math and stat part purpose. You need to download and install [R](https://cran.r-project.org) and [RStudio](https://posit.co/download) if you want to practice the code in the third part of this handbook

### Preface to version 0.5: beta {.unnumbered}

This has been a long process. While the idea of helping Malagasy in their data-analyses was born a while ago, it took years to find make up my mind on the topic, the format, and how to link different topics. While not satisfied, it is time to publish the first version. This version is a draft. Many will be underwhelmed to not say dissapointed by the fondational aspescts and selection of chapters, but I published it for the following reasons:

- Is it going in the right direction? Your constructive or destructive feedback is direly needed. You can email me directly or fill this [feedback link](placeholder). Thank you in advance for your help.

- It takes time to learn the basics. During most workshops I gave, the main problem is actually the basics which are squished in a couple days leaving overwhelmed. This version highlight the importance of the basics and allow sufficient time to digest.

You ca see this book mimic software release, and this refer to version than edition. I will occasionaly edit some parts and these will be published as version 0.5.1, 0.5.2 etc. You will only have access to the last version online and previous version will not be archived. I sincerely hope that the wait for the first oficial version 1.0 will not be too long.
